security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from documentation, sample rules, and CI snippets rather than executable skill code. remediation.suggestion: Pin Semgrep container images, action versions, and pip package versions before recommending production CI use.

semantic_findings.description: The CI examples use mutable or broad dependency references, including a latest container image and unpinned package installs. Users who copy these examples could receive unexpected Semgrep versions in security pipelines.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited CI examples explicitly use semgrep/semgrep:latest and pip install semgrep without a version pin. This is a supply chain reliability risk if users copy the templates directly.

content.value_statement: Development teams need repeatable static security review without building rules from scratch. This skill guides Semgrep scans, OWASP and CWE mapping, remediation planning, and CI integration.
actual_capabilities: Plans Semgrep scans for repositories, pull requests, and baseline reviews.
Maps findings to OWASP Top 10 and CWE categories.
Provides remediation guidance for injection, XSS, traversal, deserialization, and weak cryptography.
Helps draft custom Semgrep rules from YAML templates.
Supplies CI examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins workflows.
Explains SARIF and JSON reporting concepts for security dashboards.
limitations: Semgrep must be installed locally or available in CI.
It cannot prove exploitability without human review and testing.
Rule coverage depends on selected rulesets and language support.
The package includes guidance and templates, not the referenced helper scripts.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Security Gate
use_cases.description: Add Semgrep checks that block severe findings before merge.

use_cases.title: Security Review Triage
use_cases.description: Group Semgrep findings by risk, standard, and remediation priority.

use_cases.title: Custom Rule Development
use_cases.description: Draft organization-specific rules for recurring insecure patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a Semgrep security scan for this repository and choose starter rulesets.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Semgrep findings, group them by risk, map standards, and suggest a fix order.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Semgrep CI gate that reports SARIF and fails only on severe confirmed findings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Custom Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Semgrep rule plan for our unsafe helper pattern, including tests and false positive controls.

output_examples.input: A team wants first-time SAST coverage for a Python and JavaScript service.
output: A scan plan for local and CI use.
A triage checklist for severe findings.

output_examples.input: A pull request introduces Semgrep findings in authentication code.
output: Findings grouped by severity and affected component.
OWASP and CWE mapping for each issue.
Remediation steps suitable for the code owner.

output_examples.input: A security team needs a custom rule for unsafe file reads.
output: Rule design notes with positive and negative match cases.
Testing guidance for vulnerable and safe samples.

best_practices: Start with severe findings, then expand coverage after tuning noisy rules.
Pin CI action, image, and package versions before production rollout.
Document accepted false positives with owner, reason, and review date.
anti_patterns: Do not fail every build on untuned informational findings.
Do not treat Semgrep output as proof of exploitability without review.
Do not copy CI snippets without adapting permissions and version pins.

faq.question: Does this skill run Semgrep by itself?
faq.answer: It provides workflows, commands, rules, and review guidance. Semgrep must be available in your environment.

faq.question: Can it replace manual security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps find and prioritize patterns, but humans must confirm context, impact, and fix quality.

faq.question: Which standards does it reference?
faq.answer: It references OWASP Top 10, CWE, SANS Top 25, and Semgrep rule registry concepts.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I customize first?
faq.answer: Customize rulesets, severity thresholds, ignored paths, SARIF upload settings, and version pins.

faq.question: What outputs should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect scan plans, triage guidance, standard mappings, remediation notes, and CI integration advice.
